brief: Charles Elliot Fox was born in 1878 and joined the Melanesian Mission in 1902. He served with the mission in various capacities for over seventy years. He was a man of scholarship, courage, generosity of spirit, and humility, and his influence on the education and spiritual life of Melanesia was unequalled. His work among the villages during World War II was legendary. He wrote on Melanesian culture and history, and did much translation work. His sense of identity with the Melanesian people was marked by his spending eleven years as a member of the Melanesian Brotherhood. He died in 1977.
